page: Vultr voc-g-32c-128gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 32 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this server provides 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 640 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU features a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instruction sets.

In benchmark evaluations, this instance demonstrates strong multi-core and memory performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test yielded a score of 99997.49, placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with large-block read-only operations reaching 537.96 GB/sec and write operations reaching 292.8 GB/sec, both ranking in the top 10%. Passmark CPU tests further confirm its capabilities, scoring 63947.14 overall, with strong results in encryption and physics simulations.

Given its shared CPU allocation, this instance offers a cost-efficient profile for resource-dense workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. It is well-suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, static web serving, and database operations, as evidenced by its 73.66 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Additionally, it supports moderate machine learning tasks, achieving a text generation speed of 30.05 tokens per second on a medium 7B LLM model.
